clue.text: Although a learner, entered a card-game

indicators.note: one piece entered another means it goes inside it here

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
L is the learner sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A novice joining in a game of cards despite something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' puts L inside WHIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjunctions of concession, interchangeable in a sentence such as 'while it rained'.

clue.text: Doctor wore drab clothes

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician dressed in dull garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb signalling an anagram of WORE DRAB; 'clothes' is a noun standing for where clothes are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a person's stock of garments as well as the cupboard holding them.

clue.text: Home supporter shot in foot

parts.note: at home is 'in'
a fan supports a team
a shot is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A local fan injured in the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' means foot soldiers, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot is the collective term for soldiers who march and fight on foot.

clue.text: It used to be very painful

explanation.surface: Something that once hurt a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage 'sore afraid' meant greatly afraid; today the word means aching or tender.

clue.text: Mix up in motor-cycle trial

explanation.surface: Confusion during an off-road bike event.
explanation.definitionFit: To jumble eggs or signals is one sense; the other is a British off-road motorbike race over rough terrain.

clue.text: It's used to pass through Derby, say, with ease

definitions.text: It's used to pass through Derby, say, with ease

parts.words: It's used to pass through Derby, say, with ease
parts.note: Derby is not the city but a kind of English hard cheese, and the tool slices through it easily

explanation.surface: Something that travels smoothly through the Midlands town of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English city or the horse race; here it is Derby cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire or blade device for slicing a block of dairy produce.

clue.text: Head of gordonstoun takes leave of haggard relative

indicators.note: the head letter departs from the longer word, so it is removed

parts.note: haggard means gaunt, worn and thin

indicators.note: the first letter of the school's name is taken

explanation.surface: The headmaster of a famous Scottish school leaves a worn-out relation.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordonstoun is a Scottish boarding school; 'Head of' looks like a headmaster but just gives G, which 'takes leave of' removes from GAUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family member.

clue.text: A local pump attendant

parts.note: a local is a British pub, and its pump draws beer, so the attendant serves drinks rather than petrol

explanation.surface: Someone who staffs a nearby petrol station.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the neighbourhood pub; the pump is a beer pump, not a fuel pump.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who serves drinks from behind the counter of a pub.

clue.text: Number of the Spanish flat

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
flat means level, even

explanation.surface: A figure belonging to a Spanish apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a whole number, one more than ten.

clue.text: Show improvement with respect to criminal record

parts.note: re means concerning, with respect to
form is British slang for a police record

explanation.surface: Getting better despite past convictions.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a criminal 'has form'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to mend one's ways, getting better in conduct.

clue.text: What's needed for developing wee runts?

definitions.text: What's needed for developing wee runts?

indicators.note: developing letters grow into a new shape, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: What tiny weaklings need in order to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges WEE RUNTS; the whole clue also describes a woman who suckles another's babies.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to breastfeed someone else's infant, who helps small babies grow.

clue.text: Gunner has job, it turns out, in south Africa

definitions.note: a definition by location: a place found in South Africa

indicators.note: how things turn out signals the letters being rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier hears he is posted somewhere in southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns out' signals an anagram of GUNNER HAS JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city of the Republic of South Africa, in Gauteng province.

clue.text: Fled before the start of the storm

parts.note: fled means ran away

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following little word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone escaped just as the weather broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the start of the' gives T; 'storm' is a verb meaning to rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to rage loudly, to shout angrily.

clue.text: A common plant in spring or September

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A familiar plant that appears in spring or autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub, widespread on heaths.

clue.text: Summon attendant

explanation.surface: Calling for a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to call them over a speaker; a page is also a boy servant.

clue.text: Reportedly packs flowers

indicators.note: something reported is heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: packs means flocks, groups of animals

explanation.surface: Rumour has it someone is bundling up blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' says FLOCKS is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a garden plant with clusters of bright blooms.

clue.text: Avoids rubbish containers

explanation.surface: Steering clear of waste bins.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip a class is to miss it; a skip is a large British builder's bin for waste.

clue.text: It's eaten at an age-old celebration

definitions.text: It's eaten at an age-old celebration

parts.words: It's eaten at an age-old celebration
parts.note: age-old suggests ancient, but the party marks how old someone is

explanation.surface: Food served at a traditional festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'age-old' seems to mean ancient but means marking one's age.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet baked treat with candles served at an anniversary party.

clue.text: A tonic it may be, getting a mention in dispatches

indicators.note: the letters may be something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medicinal drink earns someone military recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals an anagram of A TONIC IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A citation is an official commendation, such as a soldier's name noted in reports.

clue.text: Running out of stock altogether

parts.note: stock looks like goods in a shop, but here it is livestock bolting all together

explanation.surface: A shop completely selling out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' suggests a shop's inventory; it is cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden mass rush of panicked cattle or horses.

clue.text: Indicate place for a country meeting

parts.note: to indicate is to point to
a point is a spot, a place

explanation.surface: Showing where a rural gathering is held.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a horse race across country for amateur riders.
explanation.definitionFit: A British amateur steeplechase over farmland is a rural sporting event.

clue.text: Set out to marry drunk!

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: Setting out to get married while intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SET into STE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed is British slang for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Barmaid argued about a pound

parts.note: a woman at the legal bar who argued over a pound of flesh in The Merchant of Venice

explanation.surface: A pub server quarrelled over a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is the legal bar: Shakespeare's heroine posed as a lawyer to argue about Shylock's pound of flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of The Merchant of Venice who disguised herself as a lawyer.

clue.text: Blow in either direction

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Puffing one way or the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow a horn is to sound it with a short blast.

clue.text: An embrace for lady grey

indicators.note: the outer word embraces the inner, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
a lady is a she

explanation.surface: A hug offered to an aristocratic woman named Grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embrace' puts SHE inside AN; Lady Grey suggests a person or the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale, the colour of ashes.

clue.text: Philosophical student in academic stream

indicators.note: the student goes inside the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river at Cambridge University
L is a learner

explanation.surface: A thoughtful undergraduate by a university river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside CAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Being philosophical about a setback means staying composed and serene.

clue.text: Avoid getting hot in a blazer

parts.note: the sun blazes in the sky
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Avoiding overheating in a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blazer' looks like a jacket; it is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun is to keep away from, to steer clear.

clue.text: Port trade

explanation.surface: Commerce at a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is a harbour town in Kent; to deal is to buy and sell.

clue.text: Be careful! The time is not right

parts.note: a watch tells the time
out means wrong, mistaken

explanation.surface: A warning that the moment is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation warning someone to take care.

clue.text: Girl is found in dreadful need

indicators.note: one piece is found within another
dreadful means in a bad state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman discovered in desperate want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges NEED to DENE, and 'found in' puts IS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Denise is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Doctor again involved on a point of sanitation

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A doctor once more concerned with hygiene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges AGAIN to AINAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Draining away waste water is part of public sanitation.

clue.text: Throw oneself into exercises without a breather

indicators.note: in old usage without means outside, so the exercises go round the breather

parts.note: PE is physical education
a lung breathes

explanation.surface: Diving into a workout without pausing for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside, putting LUNG inside PE.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to hurl oneself headlong, to dive.
